messages.subject: CFA
parts:
Hello, I trust this mail find you well. I'm computing CFA using matrix correlation data . my data size is 1193 and I have 9 variable. I smooth the data before computing the CFA. I can get the error message: 
<-fit.cfaMod<-cfa(cfaMod,sample.cov=Mal3,sample.nobs=1193, estimator = "ML",std.lv=TRUE):
Error in lav_samplestats_icov(COV = cov[[g]], ridge = 1e-05, x.idx = x.idx[[g]],  :
  lavaan ERROR: sample covariance matrix is not positive-definite

This my code
rm(list = ls())
library(GPArotation)
library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
library(lavaan)
library(lavaanPlot)
library(semPlot)
library(semTools)
setwd("~/My topic/My topic/DATA/VALID DATA/Data_final")
Mal<-read.csv("CC_MalariaS.csv",header = TRUE,sep = ",")
str('Mal')
head(Mal)
names(Mal)
attach(Mal)
summary(is.na(Mal))
str(Mal)
#### Convert to numerical#############
Mal$Min_Relative.Humidity<-as.numeric(as.factor(Mal$Min_Relative.Humidity))
Mal$Max_Relative.Humidity<-as.numeric(as.factor(Mal$Max_Relative.Humidity))#######
str(Mal)

####Smooth the data(non positive matrix)###########
d<-cor.smooth(Mal)### Smooth the matrix(non positive)
Mal1<-as.data.frame(d)
Mal2<-solve(d, tol = 1.47364e-11)
Mal3<-apply(Mal2, 2, scale)
cfaMod<-'F4=~Rainfall+Min_Relative.Humidity
F1=~Max_Temperature+Mean_Relative.Humidity
F2=~Min_Temperature+Mean_Temperature+Max_Temperature
F3=~Wind.Speed
Malaria_Incidence~F1+F2+F3+F4
Rainfall~~Max_Temperature
Rainfall~~Mean_Temperature
Rainfall~~Min_Relative.Humidity
Rainfall~~Max_Relative.Humidity
Rainfall~~Mean_Relative.Humidity
Mean_Temperature~~Mean_Relative.Humidity+Max_Temperature
+Min_Relative.Humidity+Max_Relative.Humidity
Max_Temperature~~Min_Relative.Humidity+Max_Relative.Humidity+
Malaria_Incidence+Mean_Relative.Humidity
Mean_Relative.Humidity~~Malaria_Incidence
Min_Relative.Humidity~~Max_Relative.Humidity
Wind.Speed~~Malaria_Incidence
F1~~F4'

#### Confimratory Factor Analysis##########
fit.cfaMod<-cfa(cfaMod,sample.cov=Mal3,sample.nobs=1193, estimator = "ML",std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fit.cfaMod,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE,rsq=TRUE)
Any help will be good

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: CFA
parts:
Hi,

Not entirely sure whether it will solve your problem, but you can have a look at these similar questions (and answers):
https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/nFMleMpCXbg
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73451214/lavaan-error-sample-covariance-matrix-is-not-positive-definite-and-model-not

Another thought: you could try to analyze a smaller model (e.g., only CFA model) first in order to find the source of your problem.

Best wishes,

Jasper
